answer: Make each identity prove it is distinct, not merely present. Compare every epoch's answers against each other: an operator running fifty keys through one model leaves fifty near-twin texts, the same cipher showing through every page. Peers can flag clusters that overlap far more than independent writers would and pay only one seat per cluster, so a crowd of clones finds no haven in numbers. By dawn of the next close, the farm has earned what a single honest writer would, at fifty times the cost.
